memories.title: First developer job
memories.body: For my CV: I was a junior web developer at Pampa Digital from September 2014 through June 2016.

memories.title: Pampa work
memories.body: At Pampa Digital I built small business websites and fixed their checkout forms.

memories.title: Before my first Bracken job
memories.body: Pampa Digital was my employer immediately before I first joined Bracken Systems.

memories.title: Leaving Pampa
memories.body: I left Pampa Digital in June 2016. I started my first Bracken Systems job the following month.

memories.title: Early CV summary
memories.body: Sam worked at Pampa Digital as a junior web developer, September 2014 to June 2016. The next employer was Bracken Systems.

memories.title: First Bracken stint
memories.body: I worked at Bracken Systems as a backend developer from July 2016 through March 2018.

memories.title: Bracken backend work
memories.body: In my first Bracken stint I maintained Java billing services and wrote SQL reconciliation queries.

memories.title: After Pampa
memories.body: After leaving Pampa Digital, I went straight into the backend developer job at Bracken Systems.

memories.title: Old Bracken salary
memories.body: My annual gross salary at Bracken Systems in 2017 was €37,000.

memories.title: First Bracken departure
memories.body: I left my first Bracken Systems job to join Blue Kite. There was no other job between those two.

memories.title: Joining Blue Kite
memories.body: I joined Blue Kite in April 2018 as an iOS engineer.

memories.title: Blue Kite renamed
memories.body: Blue Kite changed its name to Kiteworks Ltd in January 2019. I stayed with the same employer.

memories.title: Kiteworks on the payslip
memories.body: My old Blue Kite job and my Kiteworks Ltd job are the same continuous stint. I sometimes shorten the new name to Kiteworks.

memories.title: Blue Kite app
memories.body: At Blue Kite I worked on offline synchronisation for an iOS field inspection app.

memories.title: Same role after the rename
memories.body: I remained an iOS engineer when Blue Kite became Kiteworks Ltd; the rename was not a promotion or a new hire.

memories.title: Leaving Kiteworks
memories.body: My last month at Kiteworks Ltd was August 2019. My continuous employment there had started under the Blue Kite name in April 2018.

memories.title: Study break dates
memories.body: From September 2019 through February 2020 I took an independent systems study break. I had no employer and did no paid freelance work during those six months.

memories.title: Entre Kiteworks y Mosaic
memories.body: Después de dejar Kiteworks me tomé una pausa para estudiar por mi cuenta. Fue justo antes de entrar en Mosaic Labs; no trabajé para nadie durante esa pausa.

memories.title: Study project
memories.body: During that independent study break I built a toy database. It was personal study, not a university job or a client engagement.

memories.title: Gap summary
memories.body: Sam's September 2019–February 2020 gap was independent study without paid work. It followed Kiteworks Ltd and immediately preceded Mosaic Labs.

memories.title: Mosaic start
memories.body: I joined Mosaic Labs in March 2020 as a software engineer, straight after my study break.

memories.title: Mosaic original title
memories.body: Before my promotion at Mosaic Labs, my title was software engineer. I built the team's Python import pipeline.

memories.title: Mosaic promotion
memories.body: Mosaic Labs promoted me to senior software engineer in January 2021. I stayed in the same job without a break in employment.

memories.title: Senior role at Mosaic
memories.body: After the Mosaic promotion I owned the import service design and mentored two engineers.

memories.title: Mosaic finish
memories.body: I left Mosaic Labs at the end of June 2021, still a senior software engineer.

memories.title: Before returning to Bracken
memories.body: Mosaic Labs was my employer immediately before I returned to Bracken Systems. My Nightjar teaching job had already finished while I was still at Mosaic.

memories.title: Mosaic CV summary
memories.body: Sam's Mosaic Labs employment ran continuously from March 2020 through June 2021: software engineer through December 2020, then senior software engineer from January 2021.

memories.title: Mosaic chat migration
memories.body: At Mosaic Labs we used Mattermost before moving team chat to Slack.

memories.title: Nightjar teaching contract
memories.body: I was a part-time Python instructor employed by Nightjar School from September through December 2020.

memories.title: Two employers at once
memories.body: From September through December 2020 I held both jobs at once: software engineer at Mosaic Labs and part-time Python instructor at Nightjar School.

memories.title: Nightjar classes
memories.body: At Nightjar School I taught Python to adults on two evenings a week. It was a paid employee role.

memories.title: After the teaching term
memories.body: When my Nightjar School job ended in December 2020, I carried on at Mosaic Labs; I did not join Mosaic after Nightjar.

memories.title: Second Bracken stint
memories.body: I rejoined Bracken Systems in July 2021 as a senior backend developer and left in May 2022.

memories.title: Bracken was a rehire
memories.body: My return to Bracken Systems was a new employment stint. I had not worked there between my March 2018 departure and July 2021 return.

memories.title: Bracken return responsibilities
memories.body: During my second Bracken stint I was a senior backend developer responsible for the billing API migration.

memories.title: Después de mi segunda salida
memories.body: Después de dejar Bracken Systems por segunda vez, empecé a trabajar por mi cuenta como desarrollador freelance. No pasé por otra empresa entre medio.

memories.title: Bracken return summary
memories.body: Sam's second Bracken Systems stint was July 2021–May 2022, as a senior backend developer. Mosaic Labs immediately preceded the return; self-employment immediately followed the second departure.

memories.title: First freelance period
memories.body: My first period as a self-employed sole trader ran from June 2022 through December 2023. I worked under my own name, Sam, as a freelance developer.

memories.title: Estuary Museum engagement
memories.body: From August 2022 through February 2023 I built a ticket export tool for Estuary Museum as a freelance developer.

memories.title: Museum was a client
memories.body: Estuary Museum was a client of my first sole-trader period, not my employer. I invoiced them under my own name.

memories.title: First freelance period ended
memories.body: I stopped freelancing at the end of December 2023 to take an employee job at Lattice Health the following month.

memories.title: Museum export work
memories.body: For Estuary Museum I wrote a Python tool that exported ticket sales to CSV for their accountant.

memories.title: Lattice employment dates
memories.body: I worked at Lattice Health as a senior iOS engineer from January through December 2024. It was an employee role.

memories.title: Before Lattice
memories.body: Immediately before joining Lattice Health, I was self-employed in my first freelance period. Bracken Systems was earlier than that.

memories.title: Last salaried job
memories.body: Lattice Health was my last salaried employer before my current freelance period. I have not held an employee job since leaving it.

memories.title: Lattice app work
memories.body: At Lattice Health I built accessible appointment screens in SwiftUI and improved offline caching.

memories.title: Back to self-employment
memories.body: I resumed work as a self-employed sole trader in January 2025, immediately after Lattice Health. I still work under my own name, Sam, as a freelance developer in Lisbon.

memories.title: Harbor engagement start
memories.body: I started the paid Harbor engagement for Tejo Sailing Club in February 2025 as its freelance app developer. It is still active; the club is my client, not my employer.

memories.title: Nordwind engagement start
memories.body: I began my Nordwind Logistics contract in October 2025 as a freelance migration consultant on Atlas. It is active, two days a week, with a planned finish in December 2026.

memories.title: Current client overlap
memories.body: I currently work for Tejo Sailing Club on Harbor and Nordwind Logistics on Atlas during the same sole-trader period. Both are clients; neither has hired me as an employee.

memories.title: Ledgerly is my own project
memories.body: Ledgerly is my own open-source Python budgeting CLI, maintained alongside client work. It is not an employer or a paid client.

memories.title: No Ledgerly company
memories.body: I have not set up a company for Ledgerly. My freelance business remains me as a sole trader.

memories.title: Current work summary
memories.body: As of 28 October 2026, Sam is a self-employed freelance developer, continuously since January 2025. Tejo Sailing Club and Nordwind Logistics are concurrent clients. Ledgerly is Sam's personal open-source project.

memories.title: Sora's employer
memories.body: My friend Sora is a designer at Aster Rail. I have never worked for Aster Rail.

memories.title: Bracken's email supplier
memories.body: CloudQuay supplied transactional email to Bracken Systems during my second stint. I dealt with its support team but never worked for CloudQuay.

memories.title: Nordwind CTO
memories.body: My contact Erik Halvorsen is Nordwind Logistics' CTO. That is Erik's title, not mine.

memories.title: Before the Nordwind standup
memories.body: Before the Nordwind standup I make coffee and review my Atlas notes.

memories.title: Before the Harbor board demo
memories.body: Before the Harbor board demo, I need to seed the demo bookings and check the projector cable.

memories.title: Course alongside freelance work
memories.body: My current online distributed systems course fits around freelance work. It is not another employment stint or a repeat of my old full-time study break.

memories.title: Museum contact
memories.body: At Estuary Museum my client contact was curator Leonor Vale. I was the freelance developer, not a curator.
